quarterly_data.signal: At the TSMC 2026 North America Open Innovation Platform (OIP) Ecosystem Forum, Alchip presented a technical paper with Synopsys on how AI data center ASICs can overcome scale-up and scale-out bandwidth constraints, combining Synopsys 224G PHY IP with Alchip's advanced packaging and signal/power integrity (SI/PI) expertise in a protocol-agnostic physical design. At 224 Gbps SerDes speeds the work co-optimized escape routing, die-edge utilization (differentiated East/West vs North/South die edges) and package-substrate breakout; it extended to E/W package breakout techniques to sustain 1.6 terabits per second of networking bandwidth, and the approach is described as forward-scalable to ultimately support 448G SerDes. Alchip says engineers achieved chip-to-chip interconnect bandwidth density approaching theoretical physical limits, demonstrating the feasibility of ultra high density 224G scale-up interconnect. A technical paper / methodology, not a product launch or design win; no customers or dates stated.
quarterly_data.figure: Synopsys 224G PHY IP + Alchip packaging/SI-PI; 1.6 terabits per second E/W package breakout; scalable to 448G SerDes
